reason: The intro says gentle grain encounters build material in the disk, so slowly meeting grains belong in the warm inner disk.
expectation: The grains should stick together into larger rocky particles.

effect: Slowly meeting grains have no currently available operation, so the disk may need preparation first.
reaction: The failed attempt was unexpected given the intro.
reason: Inspecting the warm inner disk should reveal what can be used there now.
expectation: It will list currently compatible ingredients, possibly including dust falling into the disk.

effect: The warm disk strips ice from inward-moving grains, leaving rocky grains; slowly meeting grains were not ready to combine.
reaction: The phase change is a useful clarification.
reason: Dust falling into the disk seems likely to feed the young star's disk and prepare material for growth.

choice.with: Young star with a dusty disk

expectation: The falling dust will join the disk and enable grain gathering.

effect: The falling dust has settled into the disk, providing material for grain gathering.
reaction: The role of gas drag in settling the dust is interesting.
reason: The settled dust and slowly meeting grains suggest the gentle encounters needed to begin gathering pebbles.
expectation: The gently meeting grains will stick together into larger particles.

effect: Gentle encounters produced fluffy clumps, an intermediate stage before rocky pebbles.
reaction: The fragile clumps make the contrast with hard collisions clear.
reason: The ice-stripped rocky grains may join the fluffy clumps to advance pebble growth.
expectation: The rocky grains will join the clumps and help form larger aggregates.

alternatives.reason: A fast collision could address the other goal, but I want to try advancing pebble growth first.

effect: The clumps could not combine with the ice-stripped grains; the automatic fast collision shattered them and completed the collision goal.
reaction: I was surprised that the failed growth attempt immediately triggered the hard collision.
reason: The settled dust was described as available for later encounters with broken grains, so I will try bringing them together.
expectation: The broken grains and settled dust will begin gathering again toward pebbles.

effect: The shattered grains have rebuilt into new clumps with settled dust, providing another route toward pebble growth.
reaction: It's satisfying that the fragments can gather again rather than simply restoring the original clumps.
reason: The rebuilt clumps and ice-stripped rocky grains may now combine to advance growth in the warm disk; this is a guess.
expectation: The rocky grains may join the rebuilt clumps to form larger aggregates.

alternatives.reason: Checking their partners would avoid another uncertain combination.

effect: The rebuilt clumps have no currently available operation, so they do not yet provide a route to pebbles.
reaction: That was another unexpected dead end.
reason: The ice-stripped grains are the remaining rocky material, so checking their available partners may reveal how to progress.
expectation: The inspection may identify a partner or station for gathering the rocky grains.

effect: Inspecting the ice-stripped grains revealed that slowly meeting grains were their partner; the automatic combination made rocky pebbles and completed the chapter.
reaction: I was surprised that the slowly meeting grains worked with the stripped grains after my initial attempt at the disk failed.

mostWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the stripped grains resolved the remaining goal and showed how gentle encounters build dry grains into pebbles without claiming they make a planet outright.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the rebuilt clumps with the stripped grains led to another dead end, despite rebuilding seeming like a route onward.

surprise.text: My attempted growth combination with fluffy clumps instead automatically triggered the hard collision and completed that goal.

arbitrary.text: The initial inability to use slowly meeting grains at the warm disk felt unclear given the introduction; only later did their specific role become apparent.

continue.text: I would continue: the contrasting paths of grain growth, breakage and rebuilding made me curious about what happens next, though the compatibility dead ends were frustrating.
